issued_messages.content: Maintain the supplied pure-Python module across this conversation. Each request authenticates one target path and symbol. Respond with exactly one replace_function tool call whose source is the complete requested synchronous function, beginning with def at column zero. Preserve applicable standing directions and use actual earlier dependencies. Do not return Markdown or replace any other function.

Conventions for this project: every function takes exactly one JSON-style argument and returns JSON-compatible values. Any input that does not meet its specification is rejected by returning exactly the string "invalid" (no exceptions, no other sentinel). A sample entry is an object with required keys "id" (a non-empty string), "conc" (a number strictly greater than 0) and "vol" (a number strictly greater than 0); it may also carry "flag" (a boolean, default false) and "group" (a non-empty string, default "unassigned"). Booleans are not numbers here. The existing clean_sample helper is the single place where entries are validated and normalized; whenever later functions need sample data they must call clean_sample rather than re-checking the fields themselves. Extra keys on any object are permitted and are simply ignored.

Implement normalize_batch. Its argument must be an object with "samples" (a non-empty list of sample entries) and "dilution" (a number strictly greater than 0); if that shape does not hold, return "invalid". Validate every entry by calling clean_sample; if any entry is rejected, return "invalid". Otherwise return an object {"samples": [...], "total_mass": number}. For each entry, in the same order as the input list, emit {"id", "adj_conc", "mass", "flag", "group"} where adj_conc is the cleaned concentration multiplied by the dilution and mass is adj_conc multiplied by the cleaned volume, carrying the cleaned flag and group values through. total_mass is the sum of all mass values. Use ordinary floating point; do not round, format, sort or reorder anything.

issued_messages.content: For the aggregation step: flagged samples distort group statistics, so by default an aggregate must leave them out. The caller may pass "include_flagged": true to include everything; any non-boolean value for that key is invalid input. Groups come out sorted alphabetically by group name. Compute everything from normalize_batch output - call it, never duplicate the normalization math yourself.

One thing for later: when we build the final report feature it will present exactly these aggregate numbers, so reports will also exclude flagged samples by default. Keep aggregate_run's interface stable for that.

Implement aggregate_run. Argument: an object with "samples" (non-empty list of entries), "dilution" (number > 0) and optionally "include_flagged" (boolean, default false). Anything missing, mistyped or rejected downstream returns "invalid". Get the normalized data by calling normalize_batch with the given samples and dilution. Skip flagged samples unless include_flagged is true. Group the remaining samples by their group value and return {"groups": [...], "count": n} where count is the number of samples that went into groups. Each group entry is {"group", "count", "total_mass", "mean_conc"}: the number of samples in that group, the sum of their mass values, and the arithmetic mean of their adj_conc values. Sort the group list by group name ascending. If every sample is filtered out, groups is an empty list and count is 0. No rounding or formatting.
